claim: Let \(n\ge 2\) and let a coherent system with IID continuous component lifetimes have signature \(\mathbf s=(s_1,\ldots,s_i,0,\ldots,0)\) with \(1\le i\le n-1\). If each component has the exponentiated-Weibull CDF \(G(x)=(1-e^{-(x/\lambda)^\beta})^\alpha\), where \(\alpha,\beta,\lambda>0\), and \(T_{n,n}(t)=Y_{n:n}-t\mid T^{(n)}<t<Y_{n:n}\), then its cumulative residual extropy satisfies \(\xi J(T_{n,n}(t))\sim-\frac{\lambda^\beta}{4\beta}t^{1-\beta}\) as \(t\to\infty\). Consequently the CRJ tends to \(0\) for \(\beta>1\), to \(-\lambda/4\) for \(\beta=1\), and to \(-\infty\) for \(0<\beta<1\). The leading term is independent of the exponentiation parameter \(\alpha\), the system size \(n\), and the signature within the stated class.
integrity: The proof is analytic. No simulation, finite enumeration, or numerical fit is used to establish the asymptotic. Literature comparisons distinguish the new CRJ statement from standard excess-life asymptotics.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the largest live order statistic \(T_{n,n}(t)\) in the IID continuous signature model.
No second-order expansion, growing-\(n\) uniformity, or intermediate-order-statistic constant is claimed.
General Weibull-domain excess scaling is background; the assessed contribution is its exact CRJ consequence under coherent-system failure conditioning and the resulting architecture cancellation.
title: A sharp exponentiated-Weibull phase transition for live-component cumulative residual extropy
